main_text.p: tivo a longum, ut, à Poeta, à musa. Verba quoq; tertij futuri a producunt, ut, canta. Sic Antea, fruftra, infra, supra, intra, extra, interea, præterea, ultra, a producunt. Numeralia in ginta, communem habent ultimam, ut, triginta, quadraginta, quæ tamen rectius producuntur.

Secundò excipiuntur Græca in e longum. ut, Mufice, mele, gesänge / cete, walfische/ Ablativi in e, à Genitivo ei, producuntur, ut, die fide. Sic hodie, quare, fame. Verba tertij futuri, secundæ cōjugationis, producunt e, ut salve, manc. Adverbia in e, formata à Dativo in o, producuntur, ut, belle, pulchre: sic valde, fere, ferme, ohe, hola genug. Male vero bene corripiuntur. Monosyllaba hæc, me, te, se, & ne, pro non, longa sunt.
Tertiò, peregrina in el fere producuntur, ut Michael, Daniel, Sic pol, fol, & nil, longa sunt.
Quartò, Græca in Er, quæ Genitivum per Eris formant, producuntur, ut, aer, æther, character. Monosyllaba, far, nar, lar, ver, cur, fur, par cum compositis, compar, impar, & reliquis producuntur.

Quintò, Nomina in is declinationis imparisyllabæ, quæ Genitivum per entis, inis, iris, itis, penultima longa faciunt, producuntur, ut, Simois, Simoentis, ein fluß in Phrygia/ Salamis, Salaminis, ein Insel im Euboischen Meer/ glis, ein Endhohn oder Haselmauß/ lis, sauck [?] / & vis gewalt. Dativi & Ablativi plurales in is producuntur, ut, mufis, Dominis. Verba secundæ personæ singularis primi præsentis, quartæ conjugationis, producūt is, ut, venis, ab is, nescia. Velis, malis, nolis: vis à volo, cum omnibus compositis, quamvis, quidvis, quivis: fis cum compositis producuntur.
Sextò, Fœminina in us quæ Genitivũ per u penultima longa faciunt, producunt us, ut, virtus, tellus. Sic

page.notes: Fraktur (black letter) German glosses are rendered in bl; several are uncertain and were not verified letter by letter, e.g. "sauck" (possibly "Jauck" or "Zauck"), "Endhohn" and "Haselmauß" may differ slightly. "Mufice" and "mele" read as printed. "hola" in "hola genug" is doubtful. The Greek-looking entries are German words in black letter and are not Greek. No marginal notes are printed. The catchword "Sic" appears at the foot, right side.
